Passed on Linux. #194 since rewrote the test (waits for the native adapter first, prints setup state on failure, adds a delayed-setup variant). #200 found for a sibling, `native_queue_adapter_test`, that an idle cold native writer need not have drain credits until a bootstrap enqueue is admitted; whether that applies here is untested

entries.exit_criterion: The lock holder is named, then a deterministic control reproduces it. Before #194, reproduced locally on macOS only as the symptom: the unmodified base `1d208f31` failed "duplicate manifest fields stay occupied…" once in 60 (`admit` returned null), and with evidence in place later concurrent loops (about 240 runs) showed `admit` returning null with the probe `held` four times, `classify` returning `retry` once (probe `free`) and the post-retirement slot lease unavailable once. On Linux, with an extra 5.5 s control spawning a worker in a parallel isolate of the same VM process, the target test's post-retirement slot-lease assertion failed in 2 of 10 serial runs (second checked attempt observed `held`), against 0 in 50 runs without that control. Hypothesis, not finding: a fork in another suite keeps a closed description alive until exec. Production gap: a non-contention errno is also reported as `retry` (see the known-gap note)
entries.status_note: #194 bounds the fixture on independently checked contention; holder still unidentified, concurrent loops against the #194 fixtures not yet run

entries.exit_criterion: Main already separated a 5 s setup wait from a 5 s retirement wait (from #189); the shared bound was the `f7c06383` version. This branch adds a cold start with its own 15 s setup budget ("a cold worker launch is setup with its own budget…"), a retirement that never settles still failing at its bound with its phase ("a retirement that never settles…", shortened to 100 ms in the control only) and "closed-stdin worker settles cleanup while paused". The 5 s failure of the same cold start (default setup bound, phase `launched`) was observed manually and is not encoded in a test: a fork-heavy 5 s control added spawn pressure to the shared VM process and made the admission-lease flake appear on Linux (see L2). The original shared-bound failure is not reproduced. Hypothesis only: cold launch and retirement shared the budget
